headline: Next.js leads detected frameworks with 76.3% share
summary: A new study reveals Next.js is the most popular framework, appearing on over 3,800 websites. React follows at a distant second.
details: A recent analysis by directree Research has found that Next.js is the dominant framework among websites, detected on 76.3% of sites that use at least one framework. This translates to 3,863 public homepages identified with Next.js in their September 2026 dataset.

The study scanned 10,242 websites, with Next.js appearing on 37.7% of all sites checked. React, another popular framework, was detected on 16.4% of sites with a framework, significantly behind Next.js.

Next.js showed particular strength in specific categories, being present on over half of the websites in the AI Image & Video Generation and Video & Audio sectors. In the Design & UI category, Next.js held an 83.0% share among qualifying groups.

The research methodology involved scanning for recognizable clues in public website responses, such as headers, cookies, and HTML. While this provides a strong indication, the application behind a login page might utilize a different technology stack.

The data also highlights that some websites use multiple frameworks, with 481 sites showing signals from more than one. The study focused on independently matched signals, meaning the counts for frameworks like React and Vue do not include instances where they are part of another detected technology, like Next.js.

While the study provides valuable insights into framework adoption for developers building integrations or templates, it did not measure performance, revenue, or developer satisfaction, thus not guiding teams on which framework to choose.
